back: An expression whose terms are constants times whole-number powers of x (0, 1, 2, …), e.g. 4x³ − 2x² + 7.
The highest power of x with a non-zero coefficient. Degree 1, 2, 3, 4: linear, quadratic, cubic, quartic.
The coefficient of the highest power, and the term with no $x$. In $-7x^{3} + 3x + 2$: $-7$ and $2$.
dividend $\equiv$ divisor $\times$ quotient $+$ remainder, e.g. $f(x) \equiv (x - a)q(x) + r$.
Divide the leading terms, multiply back, subtract the whole product, bring down the next term; repeat until the remainder has lower degree than the divisor.

front: Remainder on dividing by a linear expression
back: A constant (degree 0), because the remainder must have lower degree than the divisor.

front: Finding one coefficient of a product quickly
back: Add the products of pairs of terms whose powers sum to the power you want, e.g. the $x$ term of $(3x - 2)(x^{2} + x - 5)$ is $3x(-5) + (-2)x = -17x$.
